validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented, NOT GEM-derived — confirmed by >=4 independent origins. Both wiki-cited sources check out: al-mirbad.com/detail/138258 (2023-05-26, Maysan Oil Co statement, live+verified) describes the exact scope — gas compression unit (GCU) at Buzurgan (Bazargan) field, transport pipeline Buzurgan->Halfaya, gas treatment/dehydration unit (GTU) at Halfaya, executor taking site handover and running topographic/route surveys with demining coordination; al-mirbad.com/detail/155423 (2024-03-29, live+verified): 'Bazargan-Halfaya' gas transport line, 70 km, meeting of Maysan Oil Co, Oil Pipelines Company, PetroChina (Halfaya operator) and Maysan Energy Ltd to accelerate it. Independent corroboration: (a) EPC contractor RASEP's own project pages (rasep.com/projects/ and ras.iq, both verified): May-2022 turnkey EPCC contract with the Oil Pipeline Company (MoO subsidiary) for a 70 MMSCFD GCU at Buzurgan + 220 MMSCFD GTU at Halfaya + an '18" (70 km) sour gas pipeline' connecting them, 15-month fast-track; (b) MoO statement 2024-07-22 via 964media.com/410898 (verified): accelerate the 18-inch (18 عقدة) Bazargan-Halfaya gas transport line, 70 MMscf/d to generate 250 MW; same MoO push in the row's own iraq-businessnews 2024-07-24 cite (live URL 401 bot-wall; Wayback snapshot verified); (c) INA state news agency 2025-03-15 (verified): GCU 50-70 MMscf/d, gas pumped to Halfaya to feed Kahla district power stations, work ongoing; (d) wattaennews.net/archives/89917 (2024-09-23 field-visit report, verified): ~70 km line, GCU+GTU, 60-70 MMcf/d, project belongs to Oil Pipelines Company under MoO. DUPLICATE: checked all 16 roster PIDs — no other Maysan/Buzurgan/Halfaya gas line; the similarly named GEM 'Buzurgan-Al Halfayah Oil Pipeline' is a separate crude line in the oil tracker (different commodity), so no double-count/relabel; the attaqa April-2025 'huge gas pipeline' piece was checked and is P7434 (Mahmudiyah-Besmaya, 43 km/42in/800 MMscf), a different project. CLASSIFICATION: commodity Gas correct (sour associated gas). Caveat: every technical source describes a field-GCU-to-field-GTU sour-gas transfer line (raw gas to processing, then power stations) — functionally closer to gathering/process-feed than a market transmission trunk, though at 70 km/18-in 'transmission' is a defensible methodology call; flag for reviewer, not an error. ATTRIBUTION: Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%' supported at ministry level — the project belongs to the Oil Pipelines Company, an MoO subsidiary (al-mirbad 138258, wattaennews, RASEP); RASEP is EPC contractor only. Third-party summaries conflating this with RASEP's Halfaya Gas Company BOOT were checked and rejected — that is the separate Nahr Bin Umar project with South Gas Company. Endpoints/province (Bazargan->Halfaya, both Maysan) confirmed by all sources; 'Buzurgan' is the more common English romanization — add to OtherEnglishNames. SPEC (each >=2 independent origins agreeing with GEM): Length 70 km — al-mirbad 155423 + RASEP + wattaennews (the March-2025 IBN piece loosely says '60-kilometer'; official + contractor figure is 70 km, keep 70). Diameter 18 in — RASEP + MoO via 964media (+ Wayback of the row's own IBN cite). Capacity 70 MMcf/d — RASEP (GCU 70 MMSCFD) + 964media + INA (50-70); wattaennews gives 60-70, consistent (figure is the GCU compression capacity, a fair proxy for line throughput).
